chunks: And Ḥarīz narrated from Zurārah, who said:
I said to Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: What is the limit of the jizyah upon the People of the Book, and is there regarding that a fixed amount which should not be exceeded to something else?

He said: That is up to the Imam. He takes from each person among them whatever he wishes according to his wealth and what he can bear. They are only a people who ransomed themselves so that they would not be enslaved or killed. So the jizyah is taken from them according to what they can bear. He may exact that from them until they accept Islam, for indeed Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said:
Until they give the jizyah out of hand while they are humbled.
And he does not care about what is taken from him until he finds humiliation in what has been taken from him, so that he feels pain because of that and then accepts Islam.

key_terms.أَهْلِ الْكِتَابِ: the People of the Book, such as Jews and Christians
key_terms.الْإِمَامِ: the legitimate authority who determines and administers the levy
key_terms.الْجِزْيَةِ: the poll tax taken from non-Muslim protected communities
key_terms.صَاغِرُونَ: being in a state of humiliation or subjugation
key_terms.فَدَوْا أَنْفُسَهُمْ: they ransomed themselves to avoid enslavement or death
key_terms.قَدْرِ مَالِهِ: the measure of a person's wealth
key_terms.مَا يُطِيقُ: what a person is able to bear or afford

ai.seo_question: Is the jizyah amount fixed for the People of the Book in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith states that the amount of jizyah on the People of the Book is not fixed at a single unchanging rate, but is left to the discretion of the Imam according to a person's wealth and capacity. It also cites the Qur'anic basis for jizyah and explains the legal and social condition attached to its taking from them.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.1670 - Hariz narrated from Zurara, who said:

I asked Abu Abdullah (Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq), peace be upon him: "What is the limit of the jizya (poll tax) imposed on the People of the Book? Is there a fixed amount that should not be exceeded?"

Imam (as) replied: "That is up to the Imam. He takes from each individual among them according to their wealth and capacity. These are people who ransomed themselves to avoid being enslaved or killed. The jizya is taken from them based on what they can bear, and it is permissible for the Imam to hold them to this until they embrace Islam.
Indeed, Allah (swt), the Exalted, said: 'Until they pay the jizya willingly while they are humbled' (Qur'an 9:29).
This means it is not about the amount taken, but about causing them to feel the humiliation of what is taken from them, so they feel pain and are led to embrace Islam."
